pull_request.title: Adopt published Build 0.23 metadata command boundary
pull_request.body:
The native repo helper still calls Build's removed combined metadata observer. Adopt published ic-build 0.23.0 and render its metadata command, capture through Memory's selected Host, then decode through Cargo's canonical schema.

Preserve the locked/offline no-dependency catalog, 4 MiB stdout/64 KiB stderr bounds, absence of a deadline and typed Host diagnostic reporting. The lock changes only Build's version/checksum; no path override or unrelated package upgrade is delivered. This remains a native dev dependency outside deployed canister graphs. Own package versions and release flow are unchanged.

Registry-only Linux validation:

- All 55 repo-tool tests pass, including malformed-manifest typed failure and lock preservation.
- Strict example Clippy and actual Rust 1.91 helper checking pass, offline and locked.
- Pinned formatting, inherited dependency checks, changed documentation links and diff checks pass; the independent runtime workspace lock is unchanged.

Full release gates, native macOS and installed runtime qualification remain separate. Producer source/checksum is published Build 0.23.0 at 2fd5539b835065cba943df43a5ef5e5a366df064. Consumer acceptance is tracked in [Build #9](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-build/issues/9); review and integration remain with the owner.


Native CI follow-through: the previous head passes all 55 repo-tool tests on macOS, all three MSRV rows and all three runtime rows. Its later macOS release-adapter fixture fails with `editor_admission[@]: unbound variable`: Bash 3.2 under nounset rejects the empty optional array when preparing recovery tooling. Keep the complete installer selection in a nonempty array, appending --check only for ordinary recovery. The selected editor, exact arguments, offline policy and retained attempts remain unchanged. The existing full consumer adapter fixture passes locally with the real prepared published editor and substituted release effects; Bash syntax, ShellCheck 0.11, documentation links and diff checks pass. Matching native CI must confirm the repair on the new head.

issue.title: Qualify consumers against the current exposed Host boundary

repository.name: ic-build
repository.description: Cargo/Wasm builds, feature-safe package grouping and retained artifact caches for host-side IC tooling.

issue.body:
## Current acceptance boundary — 2026-10-19, Build 0.21.0

Published Build **0.21.0**, source `c1a748859678588c8788d1ad713d297ccdd74c8c`, exposes Host **0.29**. Its [matching release workflow](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-build/actions/runs/39248767103) passes Linux, native macOS Intel/Apple Silicon and lint/security. These are producer receipts; consumer acceptance is not implied. Older unpublished statements below belong to their historical inspection.

[Canic PR #596](https://github.com/dragginzgame/canic/pull/596), head `e7c92f8c039a242fdbd706c082be6fed4284705d`, now targets committed main `4caeec25d` and is ready for review. The superseded bootstrap layout is retired without rewriting shared history. Actual runtime facts now flow through configured single/batched and infrastructure artifacts into provenance, CLI tests and retained internal fixture callers. After-build Cargo/rustc probes and ambient recipe reconstruction are removed. Main's published Build 0.19.0 / Host 0.27.6 selections remain intact; wider pending consumer work is not imported.

Focused Canic Linux proof: 41 build/provenance cases and twenty enabled reuse cases pass (one existing ignored case); strict Host library/test Clippy passes; actual Rust 1.91 production caller libraries and CLI binary pass. One reuse case needed offline policy inherited by child Cargo. Development Internal libtests retain their existing unused-import warning. This is not full managed/PocketIC or installed-IC acceptance.

An isolated copy of the newer pending Canic source selects published Build 0.21/Host 0.29. Its test compilation stops in the unchanged operator-mint certificate adapter: Query 0.63 removed `CertificateEvidenceLimits.depth` and the fifth `authenticate` argument. Rust 1.91 caller checking also stops at missing `RawMessageId` through Platform/Testkit, tracked by [Platform #27](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-platform/issues/27) / [PR #28](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-platform/pull/28). Keep those migration blockers separate from #596; do not claim the newer graph qualifies or silently drop decoding policy.

[Host PR #210](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-host-tooling/pull/210), head `35157164b2c054cc92747e2b57a6578bc4a4e4d4`, proposes independently optional capability and scoped-tempfile backends for 0.30. It is not a published dependency. Build needs neither; Query needs capability, while IcyDB and Testkit fixture workers need scoped-tempfile. An isolated Build 0.21 source with qualification-only Host paths passes 156 focused cases and actual Rust 1.91 all-target checking, with 51 rather than 66 Linux normal/build identities. Testkit 0.55.2 source with the explicit scoped-tempfile feature passes nineteen fixture-driver cases and its Rust 1.91 library check; its graph drops from 243 to 233 identities and retains tempfile. No path overrides are delivered as consumer dependencies. Hosted exact-head checks and producer review still gate #210.

Remaining acceptance:

- Integrate and qualify Canic #596 through the owning consumer review/check workflow; #530 retains complete-release and input/reuse acceptance.
- Resolve the newer Canic Query/Platform migrations, then qualify its actual published Build/Host graph and caller paths. Preserve recipes, error precedence, source custody and retained artifact lifetimes.
- Record exact-source native consumer and required managed/installed application evidence. Linux tests, target graph observations and producer CI do not substitute for those runs.
- After Host #210 is reviewed and published, qualify deliberate consumer adoption with the required explicit features. Do not select an unpublished sibling source as a distribution dependency.

Keep this issue open. No merge, own version bump, release, publication or deployment is included. Normal sibling checkouts and their unrelated pending work remain untouched.


## Historical boundary — 2026-10-18, Build 0.17.6

The public sparse index confirms non-yanked Build **0.17.6**, Rust **1.91.0**, source `aff79af513e7eada1a8833aaafd0887a2dc67ba1`. Its [complete matching workflow](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-build/actions/runs/39139949482) passes Linux, native macOS 15 Intel/Apple Silicon and lint/security. Rust 1.99.1 resolves #76/#77 without weakening the real-Wasm heartbeat control. Older incomplete native runs remain historical evidence.

This released producer exposes Host **0.27**, with FS minimum **0.27.2**, Process minimum **0.27.3** and locked family **0.27.4**. Consumers exchanging Host values must align their direct family. Build does not activate Host's optional Wasm parser; inspecting consumers select that feature themselves. Pending 0.18 source separately locks Host 0.27.6 and removes Build's label/staging wrappers; it is not published advice for 0.17.6.

Canic #530 / [PR #596](https://github.com/dragginzgame/canic/pull/596) remain the consumer adoption owner. Shared execution, exact cdylib selection, prepared reuse, explicit environments/recipe selections and retained facts are published. Nearest declared Cargo workspace discovery from PR #63 is also shipped, allowing the separate Canic declaration walk to be replaced while ICP discovery/no-match fallback stay local. Facts must come from the actual execution-bound observation, including retained cache-hit output, never a new post-build resolver. Source custody, special declaration execution and complete-release admission stay Canic-owned.

Wire's retained evidence/diagnostic modules and bound facts getter are available from the registry since 0.17.3; its old Git-only requirement is no longer a producer blocker. Wire PR #11 owns registry adoption and installed macro/browser acceptance. Retention/failure/spawner cuts are also published. This does not prove consumer use or native application acceptance. No sibling checkout was edited or freshly qualified in this pass.

Keep this issue open for actual consumer acceptance. Original extraction #1 is now closed with committed Build/Testkit/Canic source and native producer evidence; the subsequent consumer obligations remain here and at their owning trackers. Canic draft #596 is still blocked by its documented newer dirty infrastructure pipeline and baseline Core errors. Query #84 and Wire #11 remain open for their own current-head hosted gates.

Build PR #56 is merged at 8f04fcb, but its renderer is not yet published; Shared #273 still owns adoption after publication. PR #65 is merged at 8372b41 after its complete Linux/Intel/Apple Silicon matrix, delivering the pending 0.18 label-owner cut. Staging PR #78 is merged at c445bfd and optimizer PR #62 at 652785f after all exact-head Linux/macOS/lint gates passed, including real optimizer qualification on all three hosts. Producer #45/#61 are closed with their implementation verified on main. None of these pending 0.18 changes is a released consumer requirement. No sibling source was edited.

## Historical 0.16 boundary — 2026-10-18

Released main is Build **0.16.0**, source
`546ea074bf9d1e0847b3bdb58d7ebfa93e4fe180`, whose three direct Host requirements
select the **0.27** family. The currently selected local registry lock is Host
**0.27.1**. Consumers passing exposed Host values must align with that family.
The older Host 0.26 proposal in PR #57 is superseded; it should not be merged
over this release. Normal Canic, Testkit, IcyDB, Query and Jobs manifests inspected
read-only currently require Build 0.16. This source inspection does not establish
their compilation, delivery, release or native-host acceptance.

Keep this consumer-acceptance issue open. Pending Build 0.17's explicit environment
and recipe-selection changes remain with #72/#74/#75 and Canic draft #596; there
is no published-graph 0.17 acceptance yet. The earlier 0.12 boundary and receipts
below are historical evidence, not current dependency advice.

## Prior status — 2026-10-17

The producer boundary repair is published in IC Build **0.12.0**, source `2598a417a96834d3139751adf549126add666c4b`, with registry Host **0.24.0** and MSRV **1.91.0**. [Exact release CI](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-build/actions/runs/38947150972) passes Linux, native macOS 15 Intel/Apple Silicon and lint/security. Archive/index/VCS receipts are retained in the delivery comments.

Consumers passing `OutputLimits`, `CleanupPolicy` or typed Host errors must align their direct dependencies with Host 0.24 when selecting Build 0.12. No compatibility conversion or parallel owner is required.

- Canic's local `93c69ada7` plus incoming source passed library checking/lint and 17 declaration/cache controls, including the explicitly selected real extractor. This is registry-only local-snapshot evidence, not pushed-main, complete-release or native application acceptance. Adoption of Build's admitted-tool Candid orchestration is separate from its current direct extractor invocation.
- [IcyDB PR #369](https://github.com/dragginzgame/icydb/pull/369), head `bacd69be0`, aligns published requirements and moves the extraction owner. Local package checks/lint and the real-extractor artifact control pass. [IcyDB #370](https://github.com/dragginzgame/icydb/issues/370) owns the existing private IC Wire fetch failure that stops hosted CI on both unchanged main and the PR before compilation. Maintainer integration/native gates remain open.
- Testkit/Query have earlier isolated caller compile receipts. They are not yet fresh published-graph/application acceptance, and are not inferred from producer CI.

Keep this issue open for consumer acceptance. Detailed source/lock identities, scope and follow-ups remain in the latest comments and the linked consumer trackers. Producer #49/#50/#51 and superseded PR #52 are closed. No consumer migration, application deployment or lifecycle qualification follows solely from publication.

## Historical initiating report

The original failure and proposed first repair below are retained as history; their 0.1.x/Host 0.17 versions are not current dependency advice.

## Concrete consumer failure

Published IC Build **0.1.4** (`848ae20548527f5595ea68e7edf9cfec4f3188ce`, archive SHA-256 `e7b77dd78727b5a92d5f1d980983f96c7ac9f6bf2e402878c80e03d3f29a6e63`) selects Host 0.16. The public `ic_build::cargo::compatible_package_groups` accepts `ic_host_process::tool::OutputLimits` from that version.

Current Canic source `ce4593530` selects Host 0.17 while its lock selects IC Build 0.1.3. Its `crates/canic-host/src/canister_build/batch/mod.rs` constructs Host 0.17 `OutputLimits` and passes it to this API. Canic's current handoff records the actual E0308 qualification failure and confirms that inspecting published Build 0.1.4 shows the same Host 0.16 boundary. Updating its Build lock selection to 0.1.4 alone does not repair the incompatible Rust types.

Current IcyDB also selects Host 0.17 and IC Build 0.1.3 in its dirty current graph; its integration build/cache adapter imports the engine directly. Testkit 0.37's native tests/benchmarks select IC Build 0.1.4 locally, with that lock change not yet committed. Testkit uses IC Build as a native dev-dependency, not as a PocketIC runtime dependency.

## Smallest next batch

Adopt the existing published Host 0.17 contracts at IC Build's canonical owner, then qualify current consumers. Preserve caller-owned output budgets, command/environment selection, typed process failures, cancellation, no finite default build deadline, retained artifact lifetime and all cache/digest/namespace bytes. Do not copy limits types or add downstream conversions/compatibility engines to bridge two owners.

Changing this exposed `OutputLimits` type changes the public library contract: callers providing Host 0.16 values must align and rebuild. Under the common pre-1.0 changelog rule this is a **minor** boundary (candidate IC Build 0.2.0), not an unexamined 0.1.5 dependency patch. Own versions and release effects remain maintainer-owned.

Acceptance: all existing strict producer gates, actual Rust 1.88 graph qualification and the native host matrix; focused Canic Cargo grouping/status/truncation/pre-effect admission plus consumer graph qualification; targeted IcyDB build/cache/artifact and Testkit benchmark/retention checks. Use actual registry selections after release; keep consumer edits separately scoped. No compatibility pipeline or hidden artifact cleanup.

Coordinate [extraction #1](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-build/issues/1), [Canic #530](https://github.com/dragginzgame/canic/issues/530), [IcyDB #307](https://github.com/dragginzgame/icydb/issues/307) and [Testkit #72](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-testkit/issues/72). #530 remains the larger input-engine removal and requires its existing native/application acceptance; this dependency boundary should be cleared first.

This is a read-only consumer/release audit and tracking proposal. No source, dependencies, versions, Git state, builds, artifacts, releases or CI dispatches were changed.
